_exec_summary.SummaryText:
ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION/EMERGENCY RESPONSE
This facility complies with ANSI/CGA G-2.1-2014 requirements with amendments for Anhydrous
Ammonia storage. It is our policy to adhere to all applicable Federal, State, and local regulations. If an emergency were to occur, it is our policy to immediately notify the local fire department (via a 911 call) and request that it respond to the emergency. Incidental to the fire department notification, the appropriate LEPC/EMA will be contacted.
While we have planned for an emergency, it is acknowledged that a real emergency will be
unexpected and may be much different and cannot be ensured to duplicate what may have been
planned. In reality, the situation that develops may not happen in the manner in which it has been planned. In that event, what may have been planned will serve only as a guideline to follow.
The Emergency Action Plan for this facility describes certain procedures that are intended to
minimize the hazards associated with human health and the environment from fires, explosions, the sudden and unexpected release of chemicals (i.e., Anhydrous Ammonia), tornadoes, bomb threats or other accidents or Acts of God which might occur on our premises. The primary emergency coordinator for the facility is the location manager.
DESCRIPTION OF THE ANHYDROUS AMMONIA STORAGE/DISTRIBUTION PLANT AND THE
REGULATED SUBSTANCE HANDLED AT THE FACILITY
This facility is a bulk anhydrous ammonia storage and distribution plant. The anhydrous ammonia, stored at this facility, is distributed to agricultural crop producers in the surrounding area who utilize anhydrous ammonia for crop nutrient purposes. The system consists of storage vessel(s) with associated piping, valves, liquid pump(s), and other miscellaneous equipment. From time-to-time throughout the year, portable nurse tanks may also be present at this site. The anhydrous ammonia plant is operated on a seasonal basis (Spring and Fall). Full-time equivalent employee numbers were

computed on that basis. The plant operates a total of eight months (1/4 of the year). The FTEs for the facility is eight (8).
GENERAL ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND CHEMICAL-SPECIFIC PREVENTION STEPS
This facility complies with EPA's accident prevention rule and all applicable State and local codes and regulations. The anhydrous ammonia system is designed, installed, and maintained in accordance with ANSI/CGA G-2.1-2014 with amendments and State law.
In addition, the company has specific operating procedures in place intended to minimize the
potential for an accidental (and potentially catastrophic) release of anhydrous ammonia. The
company has extended to the responding fire department the opportunity to visit our anhydrous
ammonia plant, to participate in mock emergency simulation training, and to avail themselves of specific anhydrous ammonia health hazard information and training provided by the company.
FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
This facility has not experienced any accidental release involving anhydrous ammonia in the last five years that caused death, injuries, property or environmental damage, evacuations or sheltering in place.
THE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM
In the event of an emergency involving our anhydrous ammonia system, it is the policy of the
company to immediately notify the responding fire department, and the appropriate LEPC/EMA to request that they respond to the emergency. In the unlikely event that the responding fire
department is unable to adequately respond to an emergency at the location, the fire department with whom the responding fire department has a reciprocal agreement will be summoned. This policy has been reviewed with the fire department and LEPC/EMA.
